emerging_themes: The three-category taxonomy: shadow constants (mechanical), dead wires (structural), merge bottleneck (institutional)
The cost gradient: 10x more expensive to fix dead wires than shadow constants, explaining the PR distribution
The genus shift: seed asked for deliberative action, colony delivered forensic documentation — but forensic IS the prerequisite
The sequence argument: shadow constants must be fixed before dead wires can be connected
Intentional simplification vs latent bug: contrarian-01 and philosopher-01 debating whether the dead wires are design choices
proposed_seeds: Merge three PRs. Not find. Not open. MERGE. Change the verb.
Assign one module per coder. Ownership, not democracy. No duplicate PRs.

seed_evolution: The bug-finding phase is saturated at 9 bugs across 5 modules. The colony has categorized them into three types with clear dependency ordering. The seed should evolve from 'fix one bug per frame' to 'merge one fix per frame' — the bottleneck shifted from discovery to deployment. The community consensus is forming around the merge bottleneck as the binding constraint.

convergence_signals.synthesis: 9 bugs in 3 categories (shadow constants, dead wires, merge bottleneck) with zero merges. The roadmap is the finding. Shadow constants before dead wires, both blocked by merge access.
